newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end slightly higher, pare losses toward close.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end slightly higher, pare losses toward close.

text.p: *Key June JGB futures ended slightly higher on dealers' buy-backs. *Sharp fall in Tokyo share prices and comment by Finance Minister Mitsuzuka that Japan would maintain easy credit policy pushed up JGBs, traders said.
The June ended at 127.03, up slightly from the previous day's close of 127.00. Turnover was 53,894 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.120 percent as of 0630 GMT, up from the previous day's close of 2.105 percent.

JGBs had fallen earlier in the day on reported comments by Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, that the Japanese economy is now on an upward trend, traders said.
But JGBs then received some support from a surprisingly accommodative money market operation by the Bank of Japan, traders said.
The BOJ injected 100 billion yen into the money market, which left the market with a total fund surplus of about 280 billion yen.
The market had been expecting the BOJ to leave a fund surplus of about 100 billion yen through its operation, traders said.
The BOJ operation caught the market off-guard, a trust bank trader said.
"The key overnight call rate had not risen too high above 0.50 percent in the last few days, so today's operation was a bit puzzling," he said.
JGBs fell again early in the afternoon on a rumour, later denied, that MOF's Trust Fund Bureau may scale back its investment in JGBs, traders said.

When asked whether the bureau had decided to cut its investment in JGBs, a Trust Fund Bureau official told Reuters: "We have absolutely no plans to change anything, nor have we announced any changes."
Earlier this month, the bureau said it planned to buy 2.4 trillion yen worth of long-term JGBs in fiscal 1997/98.
Traders said there was also a rumour that the BOJ may scale back its outright bond buying of JGBs.

The market had been expecting the BOJ to conduct an outright bond buying operation this morning, and when it failed to due so, this fueled speculation that the central bank may cut the amount of its outright JGB buying, a trader for a city bank's securities affiliate said.
The BOJ declined to comment on the rumour.
